questions.question: Radiographic pulmonary edema progresses through three distinct physiological stages. What is the characteristic finding of the first stage (vascular redistribution)?
choices: Cephalization of flow (vessels in upper lobes larger than lower lobes)
questions.detail: Stage I (redistribution) occurs when pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) is 13–18 mmHg and features cephalization.

questions.question: Which radiographic sign represents fluid within the interlobular septa and is typically seen in the lung bases?
questions.detail: Kerley B lines are short (1–2 cm), horizontal peripheral lines representing thickened interlobular septa in interstitial edema.

questions.question: In a supine ICU patient, where is the ideal location for the tip of an endotracheal tube (ETT)?
choices: At the level of the vocal cords
Level with the T1 vertebral body
questions.detail: This position (roughly mid-trachea) allows for neck flexion and extension without the tube dislodging or intubating a mainstem bronchus.

questions.question: A central venous catheter (CVC) tip is ideally positioned in the:
choices: Superior Vena Cava (SVC), at the level of the azygos vein
questions.detail: The tip should be in the distal SVC to avoid the risk of cardiac tamponade from atrial perforation.

questions.question: On a chest radiograph, a Swan-Ganz catheter (pulmonary artery catheter) tip should be located:
choices: No more than 2 cm from the hilar border
Within the right or left main pulmonary artery
No more than 3 cm from the midline
questions.detail: Positioning the tip more distally increases the risk of pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysm or pulmonary infarction.
